subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB368, LANDED. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist" -> OK, GR 2). GR2's sole normative content is the RAISE, and it now happens: the generated __RunUse re-entrancy guard calls ExceptionState.FlowUseError before declining, so EC-FLOW-USE is set to exist whenever a statement executed during a USE procedure would re-enter a DECLARATIVE that has not returned control. EC-FLOW-USE is an ambient per-statement fatal gate (EcBinder.EcWrap adds it for any statement in a checking-on region, the EC-BOUND-REF-MOD precedent: the raise site is inside __RunUse, reached from every I-O verb, every RWCS verb, a RAISE, a CALL and every inline raise site, so no node kind can key it; a 'lexically inside DECLARATIVES' filter is wrong because a declarative may PERFORM a paragraph anywhere), paired in EcEmitter.FatalAmbientGates with the FlowUseChecking flag the helper reads (ExceptionRaiseHelperDriftTests proves the pairing). With checking enabled the fatal condition unwinds to the raising statement's guard for the 14.6.13.1.3 #5/#7 dispatch; with checking off nothing is raised (14.6.13.1.1) and the quiet decline is the #8 implementor answer, byte-identical to the previous emission (zero-scaffolding preserved). The exception-checking PERFORM's imp-2/3/4 handler ranges share __RunUse and its __useActive array but are selected by 14.9.28.4 GR17, not by 14.9.49.4 GR3, so they are NOT USE procedures and the emitted guard excludes them by id (if (__id < DeclCount)); an OO method-local __RunUse is all handlers (DeclCount 0) and emits the bare guard. Every generated selection path was measured, not inferred: __IoCheck (plain format-1), __IoCheckEc (the EC-model I-O bridge), __EcDispatch (format 3) and the container's __RunGlobalUse (the GR4 b outward GLOBAL walk); __EcObjDispatch and the report engine's BEFORE REPORTING hook reach the same one body.
